chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the words of God Mighty and Majestic: 'and whoever conceals it, so he has a sinful heart' — he said: (This applies) after the witnessing.

key_terms.آثم قلبه: His heart is sinful — the sin of concealment affects one's inner state
key_terms.الشهادة: The testimony/witnessing — the act of bearing witness to a legal transaction or event
key_terms.بعد الشهادة: After the witnessing — the Imam's specification that the sin applies after the act of witnessing has already occurred

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'whoever conceals testimony has a sinful heart'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a precise jurisprudential clarification of Quran 2:283. The verse condemns those who conceal testimony, and the Imam specifies that the sin of concealment applies specifically after one has already given or acknowledged the testimony — meaning that wilful suppression of testimony after having witnessed an event constitutes the sin, not mere ignorance before witnessing. This ruling reflects the Shia approach to Quranic interpretation through the authoritative teaching of the Imams.
